content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] setup with 8 analog inputs, including one expansion module with 2 4-20mA inputs, and three expansion modules for RTD/PT100 sensors, with six PT100s connected. The system has grown to reach this configuration smoothly, but after installing the last PT100 sensor (AI8), I find that sometimes the reading shows 0°C. Initially, I thought this was accurate due to outdoor temperature, but as it gets warmer, I'm noticing the sensor occasionally displays 0°C when it shouldn't, then reverts to the correct value. This only happens on the last analog input, not the others. Has anyone seen a similar issue or can offer solutions? Thank you.
I'm not familiar with this specific error. Have you checked all terminals along the cable route for this PT sensor? Are they securely connected?

I'll verify that. The terminal connections use spring terminals, so they should be fine, though the space is tight at the expansion module, so a loose connection is possible. Would a loose wire show exactly 0°C, though? Wouldn't it return a negative value instead?

If you've used the standard PT100 setting in the analog amplifier, an open or short circuit should display as -50 or -500 (-50 or -50.0°C). Are the connections between the problematic module and the adjacent one correct? If contact isn't solid, maybe the base module can't read the value. No other reason comes to mind for exactly 0°C showing.

Hi [user_name], Yes, it's a standard PT100 setup. The sensor on the previous input (AI7) reads accurately. It's odd; maybe it's a system capacity issue—if I'm pushing the limits of the [product_name] system. I'll review connections and also swap AI8 with another input to see if the problem tracks with the sensor or the input. Thanks for your suggestions.
Still, why would capacitive interference result in a reading of precisely 0°C? It is certainly unusual. Have you considered sending a support request?
Or you could swap two of the PT modules with each other.

Hello [user_name], Getting exactly 0°C for an error is unusual. If it happens again, check the analog input values through the menu on the [product_name] device. It may not be a programming issue. Regards [user_name] (translated by Google)

When I mentioned capacity, I meant memory or processing limits. My program is quite large for me, with a second [product_name] device and a touchscreen HMI networked, so I wondered if this affects performance. I'll submit a support request—thanks for the idea.

Hi [user_name], I haven't checked what the device is actually reading yet since connecting online means losing counter data, so I've avoided it. I hadn't considered just reading from the [product_name] screen—great suggestion! Thanks.

Until now, I assumed you had just one [product_name] device. Since you mention a larger project, the situation could be different. Are you sure the value drops to zero in the first [product_name] device? Or is it only on the HMI or the second one? Please clarify what's actually happening.
A second [product_name] device? Maybe the error is related to data transfer or memory usage. Which device models are installed, and are all firmwares up to date?

Hello [user_name], Sorry for not explaining in detail earlier. I see 0.0°C on my HMI, but it seems the [product_name] device is interpreting it as zero too, since I use this sensor for weather compensation and it switches flow temperatures based on AI8. The [product_name] devices are set up as network masters and exchange data with each other and the HMI, though this part of the program (AI8) doesn't exchange data with the second device. I have a few checks to do and will update soon.
I'm having trouble following. It would help to see your actual program, as I suspect the hardware isn't at fault.

You modify the temperature value after scaling and linked it to mathematical instruction B026. With flag M1, you choose which value is sent to the HMI. If M1 is 0, the temperature from AI8 is sent; if M1 is 1, the value 0 is sent. So, it's understandable why your HMI sometimes shows 0°C.
You created a tricky problem for yourself. Without seeing the code, it would be hard for anyone to guess the issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered a problem where a PT100 sensor input on their configurable system sometimes reads 0°C, while other sensors stay accurate. The issue appeared after expanding the system and is intermittent, not matching typical open or short circuit errors, which show different readings. Discussions covered checking connections, possible signal or memory limitations, and suggested diagnostic steps. The main challenge is unclear sensor feedback, making troubleshooting difficult for users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect all PT100 sensor readings to be consistent and accurate, even after system upgrades. They want the system to offer clear diagnostics and easy troubleshooting when problems surface.
